intended_object: A basis (P, Q) of the 3-torsion of a Weierstrass curve over a ring in which 3 is invertible, given in affine coordinates. This is the Katz–Mazur naive level-3 structure: P and Q are sections of E[3] that generate E[3] ≅ (ℤ/3)² in every fibre. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation (which cites Katz–Mazur 2.2.10) and the use of the definition in the universal property of the level-three normal form.
explanation:
The structure asks for the following:
- 3 is a unit;
- P and Q lie on W;
- Ψ₃(x₁) = Ψ₃(x₂) = 0;
- ψ₂ is a unit at P and at Q;
- x₂ − x₁ is a unit.

**Over a field of characteristic ≠ 3.** These conditions say exactly that P and Q form a basis of the 3-torsion:
- ψ₂ is the Y-partial derivative of the curve equation, so ψ₂ ≠ 0 makes P nonsingular and gives P ≠ −P.
- Since x(2P) − x(P) = −ψ₁ψ₃/ψ₂², the condition Ψ₃(x₁) = 0 then says 2P = −P, i.e. P has order 3. The same holds for Q.
- x₂ ≠ x₁ says Q ∉ {0, P, −P} = ⟨P⟩, so Q is independent of P. Since E[3] ≅ (ℤ/3)², P and Q form a basis.

**Over a ring.** Asking for units, and for Ψ₃ to vanish in R itself, expresses the same thing scheme-theoretically:
- With 3 invertible, E[3] is étale.
- Points of order 3 avoid the zero section, so they really are affine points.
- Ψ₃ = 0 together with ψ₂ a unit cuts out E[3] minus the zero section.

**No ellipticity hypothesis is needed.** After the change of variables the discriminant is 27(μ³−1)³. Here μ³−1 is ψ₂ evaluated at the moved P, which is a unit, so the curve is forced to be elliptic. The library also proves that the conditions are necessary for elliptic W (`exists_variableChange_levelThreeNormalForm_iff`).

**Generality.** Requiring 3 to be a unit is the standard setting for this kind of level structure. It is stated in the docstring, and the coordinate description depends on it. The definition is given for an arbitrary commutative ring R, so it is not too narrow.

**Mathlib.** Mathlib has no notion of a 3-torsion basis or level structure on Weierstrass curves, so there is no counterpart.
